title: The Broken Ember
premise: Ansel Okafor, a bone-carver who hears the dead through their carved remains, has spent years keeping quiet ledgers for the Guild of Impossible Things while hiding their gift from the guildmasters. When the border wards collapse and the stars go dark in a single night, Ansel discovers the wards were bound to a dead king's bones—bones the guild itself sold decades ago—and that something ancient now wears the living king's crown. Guided by the ghost of the murdered king and hunted by guild enforcers who need them silent, Ansel must choose between protecting the found family of the guild and exposing the truth of its founding crime. In the end, Ansel unbinds the king by carving his own name into the royal femur, trading their invisibility—and nearly their life—for a kingdom that finally sees them.
about_author: Vesper Marchetti is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing funerary carvings before turning to fiction. They write stories about people who keep dangerous records, and they insist every book is dedicated to 'the ledgers no one reads.'

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Ansel Okafor works late in the guild's bone-vault, carving a commission and listening half-unwillingly to its dead owner's murmurs, when every star above the city gutters out and the border wards scream into silence. The guildmasters seal the doors and order silence; Ansel alone knows the wards were anchored to bones the guild once sold. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: dread—the safe, invisible life cracking open.

chapters.title: What the Dead King Remembers
chapters.summary: Following the whisper in an old royal femur from the guild's back-catalogue, Ansel meets the ghost of King Aldric, murdered forty years ago, whose unfinished death lets the crown-thing feed on the realm. Guild enforcers catch Ansel with the bone, forcing them to flee with fellow ledger-keeper Sefa. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: loyalty tested—Ansel realizes the guild's survival depends on the crime staying buried.

chapters.title: The Crown That Wears the Man
chapters.summary: Ansel and Sefa infiltrate the palace during the king's starless coronation renewal, where Ansel hears the living king screaming inside his own body as the crown-thing speaks with his mouth. The enforcers corner them; Sefa takes a wound covering Ansel's escape to the crypt where Aldric's full skeleton lies sealed. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: despair at the cost of truth, then resolve—Ansel chooses the kingdom over belonging.

chapters.title: A Name Cut in Bone
chapters.summary: In the crypt, Ansel carves Aldric's true death-record into his bones while the crown-thing tears at their mind, completing the king's story so he can die whole and drag the thing after him. The stars relight; the wounded king wakes with no memory but gratitude. Ansel returns to a guild that must reckon with its crime—and finds themselves, for the first time, seen. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: bittersweet belonging earned through sacrifice.
